significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(ii) causal conclusion that, in stored-but-misanswered cases, facts are "encoded in mid-layer representations but never get copied into the residual stream at the answer position," and that moving the relevant direction can restore use of the fact. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—a distinguishable "retrieval gap"—and a mechanism separating absent knowledge from failed routing, but it remains the standard separable-representation, causal-role, and steering-repair template for one class of errors rather than a law predicting behavior across configurations; work such as Meng et al.'s ROME and Geva et al.'s Dissecting Recall makes this decomposition consequential for how factual localization and editing results are interpreted. The branches are distinguishable despite the underquantified words "primarily," "reliably," and "partially": failure would undermine a clean storage-versus-routing account and the use of mid-layer decodability as evidence of usable knowledge, although it would not select a specific alternative mechanism. In the topic-substitution check, the broad topic alone would not earn this score, but storing-versus-retrieving knowledge is an obvious first hypothesis under that topic, so the claim remains near the topic median rather than receiving credit from the general importance of factual reliability.

reach.justification: The claim names two usable handles: an internal-feature "classifier ... to predict, before generation, whether the model will exhibit a retrieval gap" and a query-agnostic runtime "retrieval nudge" that copies a fact-decoding direction into the answer-position residual stream. The classifier is ex ante and leaves an action window for gating or intervention, while the nudge is itself a decode-time control, so these could be used by model auditors or deployment practitioners rather than only by researchers explaining errors afterward. However, the conclusion supplies a procedure to re-identify fact directions and routing failures on each model, not an ordering, threshold, or scaling relation that predicts what a newly calibrated model will contain; its asserted scope covers factual, relational, and multi-hop retrieval across prompts, while the claim itself concedes that the substance may be "model/architecture specific." The topic-substitution check lowers the baseline because generic knowledge retrieval offers no such handle, but the specifically quoted pre-generation classifier satisfies the lead-time tie-break and supports reach modestly above the topic's usual post-hoc probe-and-steering deliverable.
